text: Four formulas.
You will use them again, and again.
Number one: energy.
Energy equals power, times time.
Eight kilowatts for five hours: forty kilowatt hours.
Number two: efficiency. The symbol is eta.
Efficiency equals output, divided by input, times one hundred.
Six hundred out of eight hundred: seventy five percent.
So twenty five percent of the energy is lost.
Number three: energy intensity.
Total kilowatt hours, divided by the number of good parts.
Six hundred kilowatt hours for three hundred good parts: two kilowatt hours per part.
Number four: percentage saving.
Old minus new, divided by old, times one hundred.
From six hundred down to five hundred and ten: a fifteen percent saving.
One common mistake:
for energy intensity, divide by good parts only. Not all parts.
Your turn. A motor takes in nine hundred kilojoules, and gives out seven hundred and twenty.
What is its efficiency? Pause now.
Seven hundred and twenty, divided by nine hundred, times one hundred: eighty percent.
Remember: every kilowatt hour counts.
